_comment: Known IPC registration gaps at gate introduction (F-008/F-050). Entries are UI command strings not yet registered in that shell; they shrink to zero as F-006 removes the dead surface. Stale entries (command now registered) fail the gate. create_backup_scoped / get_backup_status_scoped joined with 5f0692e1: DataManagementScreen now prefers the permission-checked twins, but the tablet shell registers no data surface at all -- create_backup, get_backup_status, export_data, import_data and import_preview were already listed here. The unscoped names stay, because the ADR #7 conditional still falls back to them when no session token exists. pick_logo_file_scoped joined the same way: AppearanceSettings now prefers the SETTINGS_EDIT-checked twin, and the tablet shell registers neither variant. pause_subscription_scoped / resume_subscription_scoped joined the same way: LicenseSettings now prefers the SETTINGS_EDIT-checked twins, and the tablet shell registers neither variant of either command. get_report_schedule_scoped joined the same way: EmailReportSettings now prefers the REPORTS_SCHEDULE-checked twin, and the tablet shell registers neither variant. The legal-entity commands were initially allowlisted with bcd1f501 while the tablet shell had no implementation; they are removed from this list once the shared command module is registered in the tablet shell. The three memo-authoring entries (create_memo_scoped, list_authored_memos_scoped, publish_memo_scoped) are a deliberate product choice, not a gap: authoring is desktop-only (the back-office manager writes Memos; the tablet's Memo surface is the display banner), following the legal-entity precedent of desktop-first authoring IPC. stop_memo_scoped and revise_memo_scoped join them for the same reason (the 2026-09-07 A2/scope rulings): early-stopping and corrections are management actions on the authoring screen (MemosScreen is registry-gated to manager+ on desktop), and the tablet shell has no management surface. All five come off this list only if Memo authoring/management is ever ported to the tablet shell. The two §J quota-remediation commands (suspend_surplus_workspace_instances_scoped, recover_workspace_instances_scoped) joined on 2026-09-09 for the same reason the memo entries did, and by the route the scoped_orphans comment prescribes: they sat in scoped_orphans as permission checks guarding nothing until B1 gave them a caller in the shared over-quota card, and this shell does not register them. Quota remediation is a back-office owner action on a tenant-level view, so this is a recorded product choice and not a gap. They come off this list when the tablet shell registers them - and, per the same rule, they must never leave one list without appearing in another. The get/set_location_ticket_prefix_scoped pair re-joined the tablet allowlist 2026-09-10 after W7-A (c53eb4421) retired their scoped_orphans entries once the UI half landed: the retirement proved the pair was a desktop-only asymmetry, not dead callers - the desktop-only partial slice (fd047cbd5) registered desktop only because tablet has no locations command surface (D37), while the shared api invokes both commands from either shell. Registering them on tablet would invent a surface, so they are allowlisted here as a recorded product choice, the same route the memo authoring entries took. The KDS routing-rules pair (get_kds_routing_rules_scoped, save_kds_routing_rules_scoped) joined 2026-09-13 on the identical ticket-prefix route: they are the config surface of todo-kds-agents-1 (desktop b7ab48870/652f18494/f8b91e5be/a63fd08b6), the shared ui/src/api/kds.ts wrappers (bac53b849) are read by both shells' bundle, and the rules editor mounts in the desktop KDS hamburger panel only - registering the pair on tablet would invent a kitchen-config management surface the tablet shell does not have, so this is a recorded product choice, not a gap. They come off this list only if KDS rule authoring is ever ported to the tablet shell. edc_terminal_status_scoped joined the same day on the EDC lane's OWN precedent: the tablet allowlist has carried edc_refund, edc_sale, edc_terminal_status and edc_void since the gate's introduction - the tablet shell has no EDC command surface at all (its only edc code is a device-bootstrap list_active_edc_terminals call in lib.rs, not a registered command), and the unscoped twin was already a recorded choice, so the scoped twin was a straggler of the 26ffd89c1 EDC landing, not a new gap. Its stale scoped_orphans entry (the gate's own first violation: 'still registered in desktop and now has a caller') moved to the tablet list, which is where the exemption belongs; it comes off if the tablet ever registers an EDC surface. open_cash_drawer and print_receipt left BOTH shell lists on 2026-09-16: b8ba7c573 deleted the unscoped ui/src/api/hardware.ts wrappers, so no UI code names either command any more. Their dev-mock handlers DELIBERATELY STAY at ui/src/dev-mock/handlers/sync.ts:19-20, and that asymmetry is the point -- applyScopedAliases() (ui/src/dev-mock/core/mockDispatcher.ts) mirrors every registered unscoped handler onto its _scoped twin, and the UI now invokes only open_cash_drawer_scoped / print_receipt_scoped. Delete the unscoped stubs and the scoped names the screens actually call fall through to a silent null in browser dev preview (the R36-02 failure mode), so these two are mock-only alias sources rather than dead code.
_scoped_orphans_comment: Scoped commands registered in a shell's generate_handler! that no client invokes, accepted as host-only. Each entry is a permission check that currently guards nothing, so this list is a work queue, not a clean bill of health. An entry that gains a caller fails the gate as stale. The memo authoring entries (create/publish/list_authored) are NOT host-only orphans — the authoring screen now invokes all three from the shared api (3fb745cf), so they left this list and moved to the tablet allowlist with a recorded product choice: authoring is desktop-only, following the legal-entity precedent. They return here only if tablet registration would leave them caller-less again. The four payables entries (create/list/record_payment/write_off) are the desktop-only AP authoring surface landed ahead of its UI: the Hutang screen is a later slice, so these commands currently have no caller at all (unlike memo authoring, which already has one). They leave this list when the payables UI wires them, exactly as the memo entries did. `list_security_events_scoped` left this list on 2026-09-09, when its caller landed in `ui/src/api/audit.ts` — it was never host-only, just early, and the exit condition recorded here is the one it met. It is NOT clean: the same command now sits under `dev_mock` because the browser mock still has no handler. Moving between these two lists is the honest bookkeeping; disappearing from both is not the same claim.
_dev_mock_comment: UI command strings that no handler anywhere under ui/src/dev-mock can answer -- the gate walks that whole tree since cb0175ce26 and reads tauri-api.ts as only its router, so a name listed here has no handler in tauri-api.ts OR in handlers/<domain>.ts and no unscoped twin for the alias rule (core/mockDispatcher.ts) to reach, so invoke() resolves to null in browser dev preview. That silent null is the R36-02 failure mode the mock itself warns about, so every entry here is recorded debt, not a clean pass. Entries appear when a slice adds a UI caller while dev-mock -- a hot file owned by another stream -- has no handler yet; the gap is recorded rather than editing that file. An entry fails the gate as stale the moment a handler appears, which is what makes the list self-clearing. list_role_holders_scoped was the first entry here — added 2026-09-08 with the role-holders slice, when the command was registered and gated (staff:read) in both shells with a live caller and no mock — and cleared 2026-09-09 once dev-mock gained its handler. It is the only entry that has ever self-cleared, which is the point of the staleness check: an entry that outlives its gap makes the gate lie in the other direction. list_security_events_scoped joined 2026-09-09 with the audit security-events UI half, and is the SAME command moving lists rather than new debt: it left scoped_orphans the day its caller landed, so the remaining gap is only the browser mock. Note what its null resolved to there, because it was not benign in the way an empty list would be — the backend refuses a Free tier outright, so a browser preview could not distinguish tier refusal from a transport failure and would always show the failure path. It cleared on 2026-09-09 with SecurityTrailScreen: the handler returns a plausible page and honors the outcome and query args, so the preview exercises the same filtering the real command does server-side. What the list still cannot see is a handler with the WRONG SHAPE. export_audit_log_scoped returned an empty string to an object DTO and mark_audit_reviewed_scoped returned null to one; get_audit_review_status_scoped was NOT a shape violation (its checkpoint/unreviewed_count pair matched AuditReviewStatusDto exactly) but was inert, hard-coding a null checkpoint and a zero count so a review could never be previewed. All three were corrected 2026-09-09 and are pinned by ui/src/__tests__/dev-mock-audit-shapes.test.ts against the Rust field names rather than against the mock. That test also caught a subtler sibling of the same class: invoke() hands a handler args?.['args'] ?? args, so a handler that reads args.args receives nothing and silently ignores every filter — list_security_events_scoped did exactly that when it was written here, under a comment claiming it honored them. A mock can therefore lie about its OUTPUT, its INPUT, or its INERTNESS, and this gate has only ever been asked about absence.

dev_mock.name: delete_topology_template
dev_mock.reason: Deletes one per-branch diagram template from the store DB (crates/oz-bridge/src/topology/commands.rs::delete_topology_template -> template_delete, behind authorize_topology_write / TOPOLOGY_WRITE). NOT hardware- or shell-bound: dev-mock already keeps a localStorage topology slice (ui/src/dev-mock/handlers/topology.ts, handlers/topology-state.ts) with graph, apply and revision handlers, so a parallel template map is writable. LIKELY OWED rather than accepted -- no rationale recorded beyond the dev-mock hot-file rule in _dev_mock_comment. NEEDS-OWNER-INPUT.

dev_mock.name: gateway_status
dev_mock.reason: Returns the three configured/online gateway booleans computed server-side from deny-listed secret settings (crates/oz-bridge/src/settings.rs::gateway_status), read live by ui/src/frontend/shell/StatusBar.tsx through useGatewayStatus. NOT hardware-bound: the mock already stubs the same store with 'get_setting': () => null (ui/src/dev-mock/handlers/settings.ts:71), so an all-false three-entry handler is trivial. LIKELY OWED -- no recorded rationale beyond the _dev_mock_comment hot-file rule. NEEDS-OWNER-INPUT.

dev_mock.name: list_topology_templates
dev_mock.reason: Names a branch's saved templates, sorted (crates/oz-bridge/src/topology/commands.rs::list_topology_templates -> template_list; needs a session, not the write capability). NOT hardware- or shell-bound -- same localStorage topology slice already exists in dev-mock. LIKELY OWED; see delete_topology_template. NEEDS-OWNER-INPUT.

dev_mock.name: load_topology_template
dev_mock.reason: Loads one template payload, None when absent or unreadable (crates/oz-bridge/src/topology/commands.rs::load_topology_template -> template_load). NOT hardware- or shell-bound -- dev-mock already models the topology graph it returns. LIKELY OWED; see delete_topology_template. NEEDS-OWNER-INPUT.

dev_mock.name: local_api_mint_token_scoped
dev_mock.reason: Signs a long-lived JWT with the per-install secret read or created on the global DB (apps/desktop-client/src/commands/local_api.rs::local_api_mint_token_scoped -> local_api::load_or_create_secret + local_api::mint_token). ACCEPTED as structurally unmockable: the secret is deny-listed and deliberately never crosses IPC, so a browser mock has no key to sign with and its token would validate against nothing.

dev_mock.name: local_api_rotate_secret_scoped
dev_mock.reason: Replaces the per-install signing secret, immediately invalidating every minted token and changing the operator X-Admin-Key, restarting a running server on the same port (apps/desktop-client/src/commands/local_api.rs::local_api_rotate_secret_scoped -> run_rotate_secret). ACCEPTED: destructive device-secret mutation whose value the module doc states never crosses the IPC boundary -- nothing faithful for a mock to return.

dev_mock.name: local_api_set_enabled_scoped
dev_mock.reason: Enable binds 127.0.0.1:<port> against the primary store's database and persists local_api.enabled across restarts; a port conflict errors and leaves the setting off (apps/desktop-client/src/commands/local_api.rs::local_api_set_enabled_scoped -> run_set_enabled). ACCEPTED: process-bound -- a browser preview owns no server process to start or stop.

dev_mock.name: local_api_set_port_scoped
dev_mock.reason: Persists a new listen port and restarts the running handle on it, the failed restart leaving the new port persisted (apps/desktop-client/src/commands/local_api.rs::local_api_set_port_scoped -> run_set_port). ACCEPTED: process-bound -- the port means nothing without the loopback listener this preview does not run.

dev_mock.name: local_api_set_store_scoped
dev_mock.reason: Chooses which store the local API serves (empty resets to locations.is_primary) and restarts a running server against that store's own connection via open_api_store_connection (apps/desktop-client/src/commands/local_api.rs::local_api_set_store_scoped -> run_set_store). ACCEPTED: process- and DB-bound -- the preview has neither the server nor a second store handle.

dev_mock.name: local_api_status_scoped
dev_mock.reason: Reports enabled/running/port built by build_status over the live server handle plus the global DB (apps/desktop-client/src/commands/local_api.rs::local_api_status_scoped), so every field describes a process the preview is not running -- the accepted reading of this entry follows its five unmockable siblings. Weakest case in the family, though: dev-mock's get_pg_sync_settings shows a statically-off shape is possible, so whether an inert enabled:false handler is owed instead is undecided. NEEDS-OWNER-INPUT.

dev_mock.name: preview_promoted_total_from_lines_scoped
dev_mock.reason: PROMO-3 preview of the engine-exact payable over caller-supplied cart lines -- cart, sale, tax (with Lua plugin overrides) and the promotion engine on a store-DB connection (crates/oz-bridge/src/pos.rs::preview_promoted_total_from_lines_scoped). Its sibling IS MOCKED: preview_promoted_total_scoped at ui/src/dev-mock/handlers/sales.ts:420 mirrors the same discount math via applyMockPromotionDiscounts, and ui/src/features/sales/PaymentModal.tsx:540 invokes this variant live, so the split is unexplained. LIKELY OWED. NEEDS-OWNER-INPUT.

dev_mock.name: products_clear_image_scoped
dev_mock.reason: Removes only the product_images DB slot assignment; the content-addressed file is left for the GC sweep (apps/desktop-client/src/commands/products_images.rs::products_clear_image_scoped). Not itself filesystem-bound, but dev-mock models no image-slot state at all -- its only image-adjacent handler is 'open_product_images_scoped': () => null (ui/src/dev-mock/handlers/catalog.ts:294) -- so a handler would clear nothing. LIKELY OWED behind that missing model. NEEDS-OWNER-INPUT.

dev_mock.name: products_list_images_scoped
dev_mock.reason: Lists a product's image assignments for slots 1..=5, ordered, which the editor calls on open (apps/desktop-client/src/commands/products_images.rs::products_list_images_scoped). Reads DB rows only, so nothing structural blocks it -- but the mock has no product_images model to list (see products_clear_image_scoped), so the gap is a missing mock data model, not an impossibility. LIKELY OWED. NEEDS-OWNER-INPUT.

dev_mock.name: products_set_image_scoped
dev_mock.reason: Full ingest pipeline on the authoring (desktop) device: reads the source file chosen through the native dialog plugin, sniffs magic bytes, enforces size/dimension caps, decodes, resizes to 512 px, encodes lossy WebP, SHA-256s it and atomically writes images/{hash16}.webp under app_cache_dir (apps/desktop-client/src/commands/products_images.rs::products_set_image_scoped -> oz_bridge::products_images::set_image_scoped with BridgeCtx::media_cache_dir). ACCEPTED: filesystem- and media-bound by design -- zero image bytes cross IPC, so the preview supplies neither the path's bytes nor the media root. Tablet registers no ingest surface at all.

dev_mock.name: save_topology_template
dev_mock.reason: Saves one named diagram template for a branch, replacing any template of that name (crates/oz-bridge/src/topology/commands.rs::save_topology_template -> template_save, behind authorize_topology_write; the payload skips Apply validation because a template is a starting point, not a claim). NOT hardware- or shell-bound -- see delete_topology_template. LIKELY OWED. NEEDS-OWNER-INPUT.
